item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President immediately delegates presidential statutory functions to the Administrator of General Services; this is an internal assignment of authority, not a prescribed substantive legal outcome.","evidence":"The Administrator of General Services is designated and empowered to perform without approval, ratification, or other action by the President"},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The Administrator must consult specified executive officials while performing delegated functions; this is an internal coordination requirement without an independent legal consequence.","evidence":"shall consult with the Secretary of Transportation and the Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The Administrator must coordinate development of an internal government plan and consult another official about its standards; any consequential implementation would occur later.","evidence":"shall coordinate the overall development of the 10-year plan for energy conservation with respect to Government buildings"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must prepare plans concerning federal buildings under their control, an internal planning obligation that does not itself alter legal rights or dictate a later legal consequence.","evidence":"shall prepare plans for buildings under the custody and control of, or leased by, such agencies"},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"The segment requires submission of a plan for presidential consideration and delegates presidential statutory functions to the Secretary of Commerce, both internal executive-management actions.","evidence":"The Secretary of Commerce is designated and empowered to perform without approval, ratification, or other action by the President"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The officials must consult and provide procurement-policy guidance only to the extent considered appropriate; this coordinates discretionary executive implementation without prescribing a binding outcome.","evidence":"to the extent he considers appropriate and with due regard to the program activities of the Executive agencies, provide policy guidance"},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"The Administrator is directed to develop contingency plans for the President's consideration, so the mandated act is preparatory planning rather than imposition of the plans' potential legal consequences.","evidence":"authorized and directed to develop for the President's consideration"},{"segment_id":"8","code":1,"rationale":"The Administrator must prepare statutory annual reports for presidential consideration, which is an internal reporting function.","evidence":"shall prepare, with the assistance of the heads of appropriate agencies, for the President's consideration, the annual reports"},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"The President delegates specified statutory authorities to the Secretary of State and the Federal Energy Administrator; the segment assigns authority without itself exercising it to determine a substantive outcome.","evidence":"The Secretary of State is hereby delegated the authority vested in the President"},{"segment_id":"10","code":2,"rationale":"The Secretary of Commerce is required to promulgate rules authorizing specified petroleum exports when necessary to implement international obligations; the legally consequential authorization will arise through the mandated later rules.","evidence":"the Secretary of Commerce shall promulgate rules, pursuant to the procedures established by the Export Administration Act of 1969, as amended, to authorize the export of petroleum and petroleum products"},{"segment_id":"11","code":1,"rationale":"The segment imposes consultation requirements and delegates or requires redelegation of statutory functions among executive officials, all forms of internal authority assignment.","evidence":"The Administrator of General Services shall redelegate the functions provided by section 101(c) (1) of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, to the Secretary of Commerce."},{"segment_id":"12","code":4,"rationale":"The segment inseparably combines internal coordination and procedural routing requirements with a present ratification that validates prior directives and actions, so it contains both Code 1 and Code 3 postures.","evidence":"are hereby confirmed and ratified and shall be deemed to have been issued under this order"}]}
